blue coral, snatched from the neckband of the beast.

scurrying creatures in damp earth. But now you are lost, or not looking where 
you go as you run. The sunlight flickers through the green leaves like the 
flash of blades.  The only sounds you hear are your own laboured breathing, 
your pumping heart and your pursuers; getting closer.

Clearing in the Forest (as a young boy)
The chittering forest all around, this is a smooth clearing of grass, right on 
the slight hill that sits in the valley. It is empty but for one tall tree, an 
elm, whose roots snake intricately in and out of the earth.

From the trees you hear the shouts and clatter of the men chasing you. You 
don't have long.

in the breeze.

events.intent: Place blue coral into purple mesh as hinted
events.response:
You place the coral wonderingly in the mesh, and as it touches the wood of the 
tree the purple strands of light coalesce and spin together, whirling faster 
and faster like a spinning sycamore seed, extending outwards, until on the 
grass in the clearing hovers a disc of crackling yellow light, a vortex 
carouselling around your piece of coral.

In the distance you hear a shout: "..light! There's a light! That way!".

>

events.intent: Enter the yellow vortex to escape
events.response:
You leap onto - into - the yellow vortex, your feet sliding through the ground 
and away, your whole body tingling as you disappear into the earth itself! As 
you fall, you grab the coral piece from the disc; your fingers closing around 
it as they slip into the light, the last part of you to go, and it folds up 
over your head and you are left quiet, and empty and still.

You open your eyes, and from a high tower turret two miles away you watch the 
running figures enter the clearing in the forest, searching and searching for 
something. You see them milling, you see their confusion, and you can't help 
grinning an impish grin. You pull straight your tunic, and grasp the coral in 
your hands tightly, your prize.

Now your next problem; how on earth are you going to get down from here?

your Grandfather's old museum so you can receive your legacy. Tomorrow the 
local paper remains untouched on your doorstep. A week later friends, then 
neighbours, and then the police search for you in vain.

But you won't know this, and perhaps it's all for the best. You step out into 
the rain - it will wash it all away.
